 2026 NHRA Pro Stock Motorcycle Round 14 Results
 | November 16, 2026 
 A month ago, RevZilla/Vance & Hines Suzuki’s Gaige Herrera was in danger of falling out of contention for his third NHRA Pro Stock Motorcycle Championship, but a late-season rally cured all of that, and Herrera is now part of an exclusive fraternity of three-time champions.
 Herrera won the season-ending In-N-Out Burger NHRA Finals in Pomona to cap off a dream weekend that could easily be considered the best of his career. When Herrera stopped six-time World Champion Matt Smith in the final, it sealed his third title in four years.
 Gaige Herrera had to fight every inch of the way before securing the 2026 NHRA Pro Stock Motorcycle title at the Pomona final. 
 By Kevin McKenna | Photography by Matt Polito 
 Herrera ran 6.683 seconds at 202.39 mph to claim his fifth victory of 2026 and the 33rd of his career.
 “Today turned into something unbelievable,” Herrera said. “I might as well retire at this point. I don’t know if I could top that. To think of where we were a month ago, I’m not sure I would have believed that I’d be standing here holding this [trophy].”
 Before he could win the Pomona event, Herrera had to tend to a bit of unfinished business: the Las Vegas final from two weeks ago, which had been delayed by strong winds. In that race, held during qualifying, Herrera defeated teammate and championship rival Richard Gadson to close the gap in the points battle.
 At that point, the momentum began to swing in Herrera’s favor, as he was also the low qualifier for Sunday’s Pomona eliminations. On the final day of the season, Herrera was able to disregard the pressure of a championship battle and earn wins against Alex Laughlin, John Hall and Ryan Oehler, before racing Smith.
 Herrera also won the wind-delayed final from the previous round in Las Vegas. 
 “I woke up this morning and my stomach was turning,” Herrera said. “It was just one of those days. It’s like you want to get it over with, but you want it to go good and you don’t know what’s going to happen.”
 Denso Buell’s Smith played a big role in the battle for the title, defeating Gadson in the semifinal round, which proved a huge help for Herrera, who officially locked up the title with his win against Oehler.
 Richard Gadson’s bid for the 2026 Championship ended when he lost to Smith. Photo: NHRA 
 Gadson was in the fight for his second straight title, but the Vance & Hines team had to perform an engine swap before he faced Smith in the other half of the semifinals. Smith won with a 6.76 to Gadson’s 6.81.
 “Even after they changed engines on Richard’s bike, I really thought he was going to perform and beat Matt,” Herrera said. “That’s ultimately what I wanted. I wanted to race my teammate in the final with the title on the line.”
 Herrera now has three titles in his four years as a member of the Vance & Hines team, and he credited crew chief Andrew Hines, along with Eddie and Jay Krawiec, for his success.
 Herrera defeated Matt Smith in the final at Pomona. 
 “Four years ago, we were in Vegas, and Andrew asked me if I wanted to stay over on Monday and test his bike,” Herrera said. “I said yes, and it was the best decision I’ve ever made.”
 While the 2026 season has come to an end, the wheels are already turning for 2027, when the Pro Stock Motorcycle class will begin again in Gainesville in mid-March. Clayton Howey has been announced as a third Vance & Hines rider, claiming the seat occupied by 2003 World champ Geno Scali this season.
 Matt Smith Racing is also not sitting idle, as Joey Gladstone is tapped for a full season on an MSR Buell, replacing Jianna Evaristo, who is preparing to start a family and will take at least a year off. CN
